summary: Fix replaces unescape+length-math with a char-by-char strip loop that never strips ';', which does resolve the entity-splitting bug but as a side effect disables trimming of literal (non-entity) trailing semicolons that TRAILING_PUNCTUATION_CHARS was also meant to catch, e.g. 'example.com;' no longer trims the semicolon into trail.

issues.description: TRAILING_PUNCTUATION_CHARS includes ';' for legitimate cases like a URL followed by a real semicolon in prose. The new loop's blanket guard 'middle[-1] != ";"' skips stripping any time the last char is ';', even when it is not part of an HTML entity, so a real trailing semicolon (e.g. 'example.com;') stays attached to the URL/link text instead of being moved to trail as before.

Approach special-cases ';' globally rather than distinguishing 'part of an unescaped entity' from 'standalone punctuation character', so it trades one correctness bug for another instead of a fully general fix.
